transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-02
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Sam Carter (Redwood AE), Lina Wong (Redwood SE), Ethan Park (Redwood CSM); Raj Patel (CTO, Nimbus AI), Maya Chen (ML Engineer), David Lee (Procurement), Sofia Ramos (SRE)

0:00 Raj: Hey thanks everyone for joining, we just wanted to get a sense of Redwood's cost model. We're looking at hosted vs dedicated vs a private deploy and cost per token is kinda the metric the board cares about.
0:14 Sam: Yeah totally, thanks Raj. I'll give a high level then Lina can get into perf and batching stuff. Quick q: do you have rough monthly usage today or target?
0:24 Raj: We're targeting about 100 million generated tokens a month initially, spiky traffic though — think 2x daily peak windows. Budget on infra is around $25k a month to start, but that isn't totally fixed.
0:37 Lina: Got it. 100M gen tokens. For hosted our pricing is per-token with tiering, and we often show unit cost assuming a few optimizations: batching, KV/prefix caching and model selection.
0:48 Maya: Quick interrupt — when you say KV cache are you talking about prefix cache for chat sessions? How much does that actually save for us?
0:55 Lina: Yeah prefix/KV cache. If you have many repeated prefixes or long sessions, you can avoid re-computing earlier tokens and save roughly 20-60% of per-token compute depending on session length distribution. For short single-turn queries savings are lower.
1:10 David: And for dedicated — how do you pass those savings to us? Like is price flat or do we still pay per-token on top of reserved capacity?
1:18 Sam: For Dedicated we do a reserved capacity contract — steady monthly fee that nets you predictable throughput. You can also opt for usage overage pricing for bursts. We typically model cost as (reserved monthly) / (tokens you expect) to get an effective per-token. For many heavy customers dedicated ends up being materially cheaper per-token once you hit sustained high volume.
1:36 Raj: Ok, so back of envelope, with our 100M tokens and $25k budget, what's realistic on hosted vs dedicated?
1:43 Lina: Roughly speaking — hosted per-token full price for large gen models might be in the $0.0008–0.002 range depending on model family and context length. With batching and caching we'd show effective unit down to $0.00025–0.0006 in many workloads. Dedicated can drop it further, e.g. $0.00015–0.0004 effective per-token depending on commit level, autoscale config and whether you accept quantized variants.
2:08 Sofia: What's the impact of latency on batching? We can't exceed 300ms P95 for our user flows.
2:15 Lina: Right, batching is a trade: larger batches improve throughput and reduce cost but increase latency. We recommend dynamic batching with strict latency caps; our runtime supports per-route latency SLOs so you can pin some routes to low-latency (smaller batch sizes) and others to high-throughput. Typical config: keep interactive routes at 50–200ms target with small max batch, background routes can batch up to hundreds of ms.
2:41 Raj: Do you have tooling to simulate our traffic and show what batching would look like?
2:46 Lina: Yes — we have a benchmark harness. I can run your 7-day sample trace through it to project P95 and cost with different batch-cache settings.
2:56 Raj: We'll do that.
2:58 Maya: A couple specific asks: 1) How do you handle KV cache invalidation if model updates change tokenization? 2) Do you have examples of cost calcs with mixed prompt+generate and embeddings?
3:12 Lina: For model updates we version caches and we recommend rolling model updates with canary traffic; cache invalidation is part of the rollout. For mixed workloads we show sample spreadsheets — e.g., if 30% of requests are embeddings, those are billed separately at embedding unit rates and have different latencies, but caching can still help if you reuse inputs. I'll include a mixed-workload example in the follow-up.
3:34 David: Security question — we need SOC2 and SSO integration plus customer-managed KMS if possible. Is private deploy required for that?
3:42 Sam: Not necessarily. Hosted can support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations on enterprise plans and we have SOC2 compliance artifacts. Private gives you more networking control (VPC peering, on-prem air-gapped) which some regulated customers prefer. We'll attach the SOC2 summary and KMS notes.
3:58 Raj: How about data retention — if we need short retention windows for prompts, can you configure that per tenant?
4:05 Ethan: Yes that's configurable on dedicated and private; on hosted we offer retention controls and enterprise agreements for shorter windows and strict deletion policies; we'll include specifics.
4:15 Maya: Back to unit economics — what about quantized models? How big is the quality tradeoff?
4:20 Lina: Quantization (8-bit/4-bit) can save 2-4x on GPU memory and cost but you might see small quality regressions on certain tasks. We recommend A/B testing critical prompts. For many retrieval-augmented generation tasks quantized models are fine. We'll propose a quantization recommendation tied to your eval prompts.
4:37 Raj: For the POC we want a clear evaluation: cost per 1M tokens with our traffic, P95 latency, and sample quality metric (ROUGE/F1 or human sample). Can you produce that?
4:47 Lina: Yes - run your trace through our harness, test hosted baseline then dedicated config, include caching/batching toggles and quantized variants, and produce CSV with cost math.
4:55 David: Procurement question — what's the minimum committed term for Dedicated?
4:58 Sam: Typically 3–12 month contracts; we can do flexible pilot terms for initial proof-of-value.
5:05 Raj: Any hidden fees? Like ingress/egress networking costs or storage for cache?
5:09 Sam: We try to be transparent; networking is usually standard cloud egress if you use VPC peering on private, but for hosted we include standard ingress/egress in most plans—will call out anything unusual in the quote. Cache storage is included in Dedicated pricing unless you're asking for huge external persistent stores.
5:26 Maya: Could you walk through an example calc — say 100M tokens, 40% cache savings, 2x batching benefit on throughput.
5:33 Lina: Sure I'll do a quick verbal. Base compute cost per-token say $0.0009. If caching saves 40% that's 0.6 * 0.0009 = $0.00054. Batching might give another 2x efficiency so effective down to $0.00027. Multiply by 100M tokens = $27k. So that sits just above your $25k budget. With dedicated and a commit we can probably push below $20k depending on model choice and quantization.
6:02 Raj: OK that math helps. Who typically owns the caching config? Our SRE or your ops team?
6:08 Lina: The config is in the control plane you manage; our solutions/SEs will recommend defaults and set up the initial config, then your SRE can tune. For Dedicated we can also provide operational runbooks.
6:19 Sofia: For PCI/PHI data we probably need on-prem or fully private. Is that accurate?
6:24 Sam: Yes many customers with PHI/PCI prefer Private deployments. We support private control plane and on-prem packages. We'll include a matrix of features per deployment type in the follow-up.
6:36 David: What's the SLA on Dedicated?
6:39 Sam: We offer SLA-backed uptime and latency targets for Dedicated enterprise contracts; specifics are in the enterprise addendum.
6:45 Raj: Any references of customers with similar volumes and budgets?
6:49 Sam: We have a few fintech and health customers at similar volumes; I'll share anonymized case studies and a short reference list.
6:58 Maya: For the benchmark harness — what's the turnaround time?
7:02 Lina: If you give us the 7-day trace and prompt sets, we can run an initial hosted vs dedicated projection in 3–5 business days. Full POC (benchmarks + A/B quality evals) takes 2–3 weeks depending on scope.
7:17 Raj: Sounds good.
7:19 Sam: Next steps recap: we'll send pricing and cost calc, Lina will send benchmark harness and batching/caching docs, Ethan will include SOC2 + KMS notes, Maya will send traffic sample, and we'll schedule a 2-hr POC scoping session next week.
7:33 Raj: Great. Thanks everyone.
7:35 End meeting.
